subject: Post-demo: Deployment path recommendation & quickstart questions
messages:

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: Deployment path recommendation & quickstart questions

Jamie — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so the PayFlux team can run a Hosted API evaluation this week.

TL;DR recommendation
- For the first 2–4 week functional evaluation we recommend Hosted API (fastest onboarding, no infra ops). If you need guaranteed isolation or very high sustained throughput after evaluation, we can scope Dedicated. Private VPC is available for later-stage procurement.

What we covered and what we'll deliver
- Quickstart: sandbox API key, two endpoints (generation + chat), example client, and a small test harness for your throughput profile.
- Rate limits: default hosted cap is 100 requests/sec (rps) per account, burstable to 200 rps with a short warmup. We can provision higher rate caps for evaluation if you share expected peak concurrency and average token sizes.
- Latency: typical P95 for the gen endpoint is 120–250ms for 512-token requests on our curated small/med models; larger models will be higher.
- Data handling: Hosted API does not share customer data between tenants. We can enable optional retention controls for evaluation.
- Compliance: attached is a one-pager SOC2 summary and our standard MA plan.

Action items for PayFlux (please reply inline):
1) Target evaluation dates (preferred window next week?)
2) Peak concurrent requests and average prompt+response token sizes (sample workload helps us size ratecaps)
3) Any non-negotiable security requirements (e.g., VPC-only, on-prem storage) that would force us to go Dedicated/Private up-front

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, pricing-commit-options.csv

If it helps, we can schedule a short ops deep-dive (30m) to walk through endpoints, sample calls, and rate-limit tuning. I copied Monica (infrastructure) and Lauren (account exec) to coordinate.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — useful recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

- Can you confirm the default hosted rate caps in more explicit terms? We need to know per-minute and per-second limits and whether there are token-based throttles as well. Peak we expect ~600 concurrent small requests (avg 120 tokens total), but that’s bursty — sustained QPS likely much lower.
- What are the exact endpoints and authentication flow (API key vs service account)? Will we get separate keys for test vs prod?
- Data residency: PayFlux is based in the US but we still have a requirement to keep logs in-region. Can Redwood guarantee log retention in US-only infra during evaluation?
- SOC2: can you send the detailed SOC2 report or an auditor contact? The one-pager is a helpful start but procurement will request the standard attestation.

We'd like to do the evaluation next Tuesday/Wednesday window if that works. Please loop in your infra folks so we can get the ops Q&A scheduled.

—Jamie

Hi Jamie — Monica here (infra). Short answers below and next steps at the bottom. I've attached our SOC2 attestation stub and the Hosted ops note.

Hosted rate caps (defaults & burst)
- Per-second: 100 rps default.
- Per-minute: 5,000 rpm default.
- Token throttles: no hard token-based throttle for the Hosted product; we apply request-level throttles and enforce sustained throughput limits per account.
- Burst strategy: for a short evaluation spike (your ~600 concurrent small requests), we recommend a gradual warmup over 5–10 minutes. For a one-off 2–4 hour stress window we can pre-provision a temporary ratecap increase to 1,000 rps for the evaluation window (requires a ticket / 48h notice for allocation).

Endpoints & auth
- Gen endpoint (example): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Chat endpoint (example): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
- Auth: API key header x-api-key: <key>. We issue sandbox/test keys tied to the account and a separate production key after you move beyond evaluation. Keys are managed from the Console with per-key scopes.

Data residency / logs
- We can store logs and audit trails in US-only regions for the evaluation window; I attached a short note describing the retention controls and how to request US-only enforcement. For procurement: we can provide a written statement covering US-only retention for the eval period.

SOC2 & attestation
- Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and an attestation stub for procurement. For a full SOC2 report we provide an auditor contact under NDA — happy to route that request internally once procurement confirms NDA.

Next steps & scheduling
- Book a 30-minute ops deep-dive: https://calendly.com/redwood/ops-deep-dive-30m (we have slots Tues 9/22 and Wed 9/23)
- If you confirm the 2–4 hour stress window and target test date, Priyom will open a provisioning ticket to bump ratecaps for the window.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, payflux-multiparty-ma-plan.xlsx

Happy to jump on a call and walk through the sample calls and rate-limit tuning.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Infrastructure Solutions, Redwood Inference
